hints: Integrate ln(3x) by parts with u=ln(3x) and dv=dx.
Use d/dx[ln(3x)]=1/x, then apply the bounds 1 and 2 to the complete primitive.
Combine logarithms into ln b and leave the result in the required integer form a+ln b.
walkthrough:
Set up integration by parts for $\int \ln(3x)\,\mathrm{d}x$:
$$u = \ln(3x) \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{3x} \cdot 3 = \dfrac{1}{x}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = 1 \implies v = x$$

Apply the integration by parts formula $\int u \, \dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x = uv - \int v \, \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x$:
$$\int \ln(3x)\,\mathrm{d}x = x\ln(3x) - \int x\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = x\ln(3x) - \int 1\,\mathrm{d}x = x\ln(3x) - x$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$(2\ln(6) - 2) - (\ln(3) - 1) = 2\ln(6) - \ln(3) - 2 + 1 = 2\ln(6) - \ln(3) - 1$$

Combine the logarithmic terms using power and quotient laws:
$$2\ln(6) - \ln(3) = \ln\left(6^2\right) - \ln(3) = \ln(36) - \ln(3) = \ln\left(\dfrac{36}{3}\right) = \ln(12)$$

State the exact answer in the required form $a + \ln b$:
$$-1 + \ln(12) \quad (\text{where } a = -1, \; b = 12)$$

ai_rubric.Integration by Parts: Integration by parts gives $Ax\ln3x+\int B\,dx$. Substitutes limits in an expression of the form $Ax\ln3x+Bx$. Concludes with $-1+\ln12$.
